doc.title: Eddie Bert interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Writing tunes and composer royalties
summary: Little Train and tiny BMI checks.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Cool. Tell me about, you’ve written a few tunes too in your life. And they’ve been, most of them inspired by particular things?

Well when I was going to school I used to ride the subway and you’d hear the click clack and all that, so I wrote a thing called “Little Train.” Things like that. But in fact I have an album I’ll give you that I made with just bass and most of the tunes that I wrote are on it, and Don Sickler, who is a publisher, put out a lead sheet book, so you can have that if you want.
Excellent. When you did your tunes, your recordings, back in the 50s, if you had put your own tune on it, you’d get a little extra money?
Naa. Once in a while I see, like I get a check with a whole bunch of countries listed, and a check for like $4.95 or something. BMI.
But I guess I’m lucky to get anything. So they’re still playing them somewhere.
